title: What an AI Receptionist Actually Does (and Doesn't)

slides.headline: What an AI receptionist ACTUALLY does
slides.body: (and what the hype guys won't tell you it doesn't)

slides.headline: ✅ DOES: Answer every call. Every time.
slides.body: 2am no-cool call, Sunday, Christmas, all 5 lines at once. Home-service shops miss ~27% of calls. An AI receptionist misses zero.

slides.headline: ✅ DOES: Ask the right questions
slides.body: Name, address, what's the system doing, is anyone in the house without AC. It follows YOUR intake script — and never forgets a question at 11pm.

slides.headline: ✅ DOES: Book the job and text you
slides.body: Puts the call on the schedule, texts the customer a confirmation, sends you or your CSR a summary. Caller never hits voicemail — the 85% who'd hang up stay yours.

slides.headline: ❌ DOESN'T: Diagnose a system
slides.body: It's not a tech and shouldn't play one. Anything technical gets routed to a human — your on-call tech or a morning callback, your rules.

slides.headline: ❌ DOESN'T: Replace your CSR
slides.body: It catches what she physically can't: after-hours, overflow, both-lines-busy. Your CSR keeps the daytime relationships — and stops getting calls at dinner.

slides.headline: It's not magic. It's a net under the phone.
slides.body: At $500–$1,200 per missed call, the question isn't "is AI cool." It's "how many calls fell through last month?" Tomorrow I'm posting a real recording of one booking a no-cool call at 11pm. Follow so you hear it.
